title: CloudFront Cache Hit Ratio and Origin Errors

controlTest.positiveScenario: Replay sample `aws:cloudwatch` events with `namespace="AWS/CloudFront" (metric_name="4xxErrorRate" OR metric_name="5xxErrorRate" OR metric_name="BytesDownloaded")` into `index=aws`. Confirm UC-4.1.23 returns >=1 row and the alert fires.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Replay benign `aws:cloudwatch` traffic without `namespace="AWS/CloudFront" (metric_name="4xxErrorRate" OR metric_name="5xxErrorRate" OR metric_name="BytesDownloaded")`. Confirm UC-4.1.23 returns zero rows and the alert does not fire.

dataSources: `index=aws` sourcetype=`aws:cloudwatch` collected via `Splunk_TA_aws`; validate ingest with `| stats count by sourcetype`.
spl:
index=aws sourcetype="aws:cloudwatch" namespace="AWS/CloudFront" (metric_name="4xxErrorRate" OR metric_name="5xxErrorRate" OR metric_name="BytesDownloaded")
| table _time metric_name namespace unit average maximum
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.1.23_cloudfront_cache_hit_rat_23"
| sort -_time
description: UC-4.1.23 — CloudFront Cache Hit Ratio and Origin Errors: queries AWS `aws:cloudwatch` for search criteria `namespace="AWS/CloudFront" (metric_name="4xxErrorRate" OR metric_name="5xxErrorRate" OR me` and returns actor, resource, and region context for performance review and change validation.
value: At the AWS edge, request anomalies may indicate scraping, credential stuffing, or WAF bypass attempts before origin servers are overwhelmed. UC-4.1.23 drives high-priority performance alerting before customer-impacting drift.
implementation: Enable CloudFront metrics in CloudWatch. Optionally enable standard logging to S3 for request-level analysis. Calculate cache hit ratio from requests (Hit vs Miss). Alert on 5xxErrorRate > 1%.
visualization: Line chart (4xx/5xx rate, bytes), Gauge (cache hit %), Table by distribution.

dataModelAcceleration: Performance: enable if `aws:cloudwatch` (or your metric store) is mapped to CIM Performance, or use `mstats` on the same CloudWatch metrics. Enable Data Model Acceleration for the CIM data models in `cimModels` once `Splunk_TA_aws` (and any CIM tags/aliases) map your fields; otherwise the `cimSpl` summary search may be empty. Step 2 on raw or metric indexes stays primary for most sites.
knownFalsePositives: Planned deploys, game-day tests, and vendor maintenance that you expect to move CPU, error, or lag metrics; compare with the change window.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Splunk Enterprise or Splunk Cloud with search access to `index=aws`.
• Install and configure `Splunk_TA_aws` with the modular input for `aws:cloudwatch`.
• Prerequisite crawl UC(s): UC-4.1.78.
• Confirm field extractions in `props.conf` for `metric_name` and related actor fields.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Enable CloudFront metrics in CloudWatch. Optionally enable standard logging to S3 for request-level analysis. Calculate cache hit ratio from requests (Hit vs Miss). Alert on 5xxErrorRate > 1%.
Validate ingest before alerting:
```spl
index=aws sourcetype="aws:cloudwatch" | stats count by sourcetype
```

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
```spl
index=aws sourcetype="aws:cloudwatch" namespace="AWS/CloudFront" (metric_name="4xxErrorRate" OR metric_name="5xxErrorRate" OR metric_name="BytesDownloaded")
| table _time metric_name namespace unit average maximum
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.1.23_cloudfront_cache_hit_rat_23"
| sort -_time
```

Understanding this SPL
Scopes `aws:cloudwatch` in `index=aws` to detect cloudfront cache hit ratio and origin errors. Tune thresholds to your change cadence; exclude break-glass principals and sandbox accounts via a lookup.

Step 3 — Validate
Compare to the Amazon CloudWatch console Metrics for the same 24-hour window. Confirm row counts and `metric_name` values match the vendor console. Run `| fieldsummary` on a 1-hour sample to verify extractions.

Step 4 — Operationalize and troubleshoot
Save as `4_1_23_alert` with severity aligned to `high` criticality. Dashboard: Line chart (4xx/5xx rate, bytes), Gauge (cache hit %), Table by distribution..
Failure modes: (1) no events — verify modular input/API credentials and index routing; (2) empty actor fields — upgrade `Splunk_TA_aws` and review alias mappings; (3) API throttling — reduce poll frequency or enable queue buffering; (4) alert fatigue — tune thresholds and document exclusions in knownFalsePositives.
grandmaExplanation: We watch cloud logs for signs of cloudfront cache hit ratio and origin errors so your team catches problems in your online services before customers or auditors do.
